class.name: TerrainData
class.brief_description: The heightmap and texture control map for a [Terrain3D].
class.description: [TerrainData] is the actual "world" a [Terrain3D] renders and collides with: a square grid of [member resolution] × [member resolution] height samples spaced [member vertex_spacing] meters apart, plus a control map that drives which [TerrainLayer]s are blended where (see [method get_control] and [Terrain3D]'s description for how the control map's channels are used). This resource holds and serializes the data; it does not render anything or know about any particular [Terrain3D] node (several nodes could even share one [TerrainData], though editing it from one would then affect all of them). Assign it to a [Terrain3D]'s [member Terrain3D.terrain_data] to render and sculpt it. Heights can be authored by hand with [method set_height]/[method set_height_region], generated procedurally with those same methods, or imported from a grayscale [Image] with [method import_heightmap]. A [Terrain3D] using this resource stays in sync either way (it also notices edits made directly through this resource, e.g. from a script, or from another [Terrain3D] sharing it), but prefer going through [Terrain3D]'s own [method Terrain3D.sculpt], [method Terrain3D.set_height_region], and [method Terrain3D.paint_layer] instead of this resource's methods directly when a [Terrain3D] is already using it: those know exactly which region changed and only rebuild that, while an edit made directly through this resource makes every [Terrain3D] using it rebuild its rendered chunks, texture, and collision shape from scratch.

method.name: fill_height
method.description: Sets every height sample to [param height], for example to reset the terrain to a flat plane.

method.name: get_control
method.description: Returns the control value at height sample [param x], [param z] (out-of-range coordinates are clamped to the valid range) as a [Color]: red is the base [TerrainLayer] index (0-255) divided by 255, green is the overlay layer index divided by 255, blue is the blend factor between them (0 is pure base, 1 is pure overlay), and alpha is the hole flag (0 or 1; see [method is_hole]).

method.name: get_control_region
method.description: Returns the control values covering [param region] (in height sample coordinates), row-major with X varying fastest, the same layout [method set_control_region] expects back.

method.name: get_height
method.description: Returns the height at sample [param x], [param z], in world units. Out-of-range coordinates are clamped to the valid range, which is a convenient way to sample one step past the edge (e.g. for computing normals) without special-casing the border.

method.name: get_height_at_position
method.description: Returns the terrain height at the arbitrary local-space position [param local_xz] (X and Z; local to whatever [Terrain3D] this data is assigned to), bilinearly interpolated between the surrounding height samples. Useful for gameplay queries like snapping an object to the ground.

method.name: get_height_region
method.description: Returns the heights covering [param region] (in height sample coordinates: [member Rect2i.position] is the starting [code](x, z)[/code] sample and [member Rect2i.size] is how many samples to read in each direction), row-major with X varying fastest, the same layout [method set_height_region] expects back. Useful for snapshotting a region before an edit (e.g. to implement undo).

method.name: get_normal
method.description: Returns the surface normal at height sample [param x], [param z], estimated from the heights of its four neighboring samples.

method.name: get_normal_at_position
method.description: Returns the terrain surface normal at the arbitrary local-space position [param local_xz], bilinearly interpolated between the surrounding samples' normals. See [method get_height_at_position].

method.name: get_size
method.description: Returns the terrain's world-space size along one edge: [code](resolution - 1) * vertex_spacing[/code]. The terrain is always square.

method.name: import_heightmap
method.description: Replaces the heightmap by importing [param image], which must be square and uncompressed. [member resolution] is set to the image's size, and each pixel's red channel (expected to be in the [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code] range, as with a normal grayscale heightmap image) is linearly mapped from [param height_min] to [param height_max] to produce that sample's height. [b]Prefer an EXR or HDR source image over PNG or any lossy format (e.g. JPEG):[/b] Godot always decodes a loaded PNG (even a 16-bit one) to 8 bits per channel, i.e. only 256 distinct heights across the whole [param height_min]-[param height_max] range, and a lossy format's compression artifacts become actual bumps in the terrain surface on top of that. EXR and HDR decode to real floating-point precision instead. Check [member Image.format] after loading if you need to detect this in a script; [constant Image.FORMAT_RF], [constant Image.FORMAT_RH], and their multi-channel/[constant Image.FORMAT_RGBE9995] variants are the high-precision ones.

method.name: is_hole
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if height sample [param x], [param z] is flagged as a hole (see [method Terrain3D.set_hole]). A [Terrain3D] omits the geometry around a hole entirely, rather than just hiding it, so holes can be used for cave entrances and similar openings that the camera and physics bodies can pass through.

method.name: set_control
method.description: Sets the control value at height sample [param x], [param z] (out-of-range coordinates are ignored) to [param control]; see [method get_control] for the channel layout. Does not emit [signal Resource.changed]; callers making many edits should call [method Resource.emit_changed] once afterwards, or use [method set_control_region] instead.

method.name: set_control_region
method.description: Writes [param control] (in the same row-major layout [method get_control_region] returns) into [param region] (in height sample coordinates) and emits [signal Resource.changed] once.

method.name: set_height
method.description: Sets the height at sample [param x], [param z] (out-of-range coordinates are ignored) to [param height], in world units. Does not emit [signal Resource.changed]; callers making many edits (e.g. procedural generation) should call [method Resource.emit_changed] once afterwards, or use [method set_height_region] instead.

method.name: set_height_region
method.description: Writes [param heights] (in the same row-major layout [method get_height_region] returns) into [param region] (in height sample coordinates) and emits [signal Resource.changed] once.

members.member: The number of height samples along each edge of the terrain (it is always square). Changing this resets both the heightmap and the control map to their default (flat, layer-less) state, so it should generally be set once before authoring a terrain rather than changed afterwards. See [method get_size] for the resulting world-space size.

The distance, in meters, between two adjacent height samples. Lower values pack more geometric detail into the same world-space area at the cost of a much larger [member resolution] being needed to cover it.
